messages:
david-cust: Hey team — hitting a weird streaming hang in prod. Python SDK generator yields the first few chunks then just never finishes or raises. No errors in app logs, connection stays open.

ben-support: Thanks for the heads-up, david. Can you paste the SDK version + a minimal snippet of how you call stream? Also any HTTP logs?

carla-eng: FWIW we've seen a different bug where mid-stream auth failures left the iterator open. Could be related.

alice-devex: Quick ask: any proxy or env var that could be rewriting responses?

 d a v i d - c u s t: (pasting minimal repro + header snippet)
```
# client from redwood_inference import Client
c = Client(api_key=os.environ['RW_KEY'])
for chunk in c.stream("/v1/generate", {"prompt":"hello"}):
    sys.stdout.write(chunk.text)
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Content-Type: text/event-stream
...

---- last received bytes (from tcpdump) ----
data: {"delta":"Hello"}

data: {"delta":" wor"
# stream stops here (no terminating double-newline for that event)
```

ben-support: Got it. Two things jump out: (1) your SDK version? (2) I see a 200 then the event ends mid-token — do you have any auth refresh or key rotation happening?

 david-cust: SDK == redwood-inference==0.6.2. No deliberate rotation but we do use an internal sidecar that refreshes keys on schedule. We also sometimes see a trailing 401 in tcpdump ~6s after the partial chunk: `HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized` in a new chunk.

carla-eng: That pattern (200 stream -> partial event -> 401 chunk) is odd. If the server switches to 401 mid-stream and the client parser expects a canonical SSE delimiter, it can get stuck waiting for the rest of the event.

alice-devex: Can you run a quick repro with `curl -v --no-buffer` to confirm tcp framing? Example we ask customers to run:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream/generate
```
Look for the status line and interleaved chunks.

ben-support: Also, please run with SDK env `RW_PY_SSE_DEBUG=1` and share logs. That turns on low-level SSE debug parsing in 0.6.x builds.

 david-cust: Attached curl output (trimmed):
```
> GET /v1/stream/generate HTTP/1.1
> Authorization: Bearer ***
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< transfer-encoding: chunked
< content-type: text/event-stream
data: {"delta":"Hi"}

data: {"delta":" there"}

(data keeps flowing)
< HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
< content-type: application/json
{"error":"token revoked"}
```

carla-eng: Ah — server is sending a new status line mid-body (some proxies or upstreams do this when switching backends). The Python SSE iterator in 0.6.2 does not handle an in-band 401 status and fails to close the generator; it just leaves the read loop waiting for delimiters.

ben-support: Action items: (1) temporary workaround: rotate key so backend accepts, or avoid sidecar refresh. (2) Try the patched client build `0.6.4rc1` which we have a fix for mid-stream status frames. (3) If you can't upgrade, we can suggest a small app-level timeout around the generator to force exit.

alice-devex: Sample quick patch for an app-level wrapper: 
```
import threading
it = c.stream(...)
res = []
finished = False

def consume():
  try:
    for x in it:
      res.append(x)
  finally:
    finished = True

th = threading.Thread(target=consume, daemon=True)
th.start()
th.join(timeout=10)
if not finished:
  # fallback/abort
  raise RuntimeError("stream timed out")
```

 david-cust: Thanks. We can try 0.6.4rc1. If it still repros we'll capture a pcap and redact keys.

carla-eng: Meanwhile I'll file an internal ticket to pin the SSE parser to tolerate an in-band status switch and ensure generator closes with an appropriate exception (401 -> AuthenticationError).

deploy-bot: 📢 rollout staged: 0.6.4rc1 deployed to canary infra for stream parser fix. Monitor for errors.

ben-support: Please update this thread after you test rc1. If you can include RW_PY_SSE_DEBUG logs that will help us confirm the fix. :thumbsup:
